name: Washington
feeText: King County Superior Court Clerk: Dissolution of Marriage $364.00 (RCW 36.18.020(2),(5),(6); RCW 36.18.016(2)(b); RCW 36.18.016(15)). The statewide statutory part is $200 (RCW 36.18.020(2)(a)) + $40 surcharge (36.18.020(5)(c)) + $50 surcharge (36.18.020(6)) + $54 dissolution fee (36.18.016(2)(b)) = $344; counties may add up to $20 for a courthouse facilitator program (RCW 26.12.240).

otherFees.what: Counter Petition in a Domestic Relations Action (King County)
Statewide statutory base for a dissolution petition before county surcharges (RCW 36.18.020 + 36.18.016(2)(b))

waiver.name: Motion and Declaration for Waiver of Civil Fees and Surcharges (WPF GR 34.0100) with Order Re Waiver (WPF GR 34.0500)

residency.text: No minimum residence period: the petitioner must be a resident of Washington, a member of the armed forces stationed in Washington, or married to such a person (RCW 26.09.030).

waitingPeriod.text: The court may enter a decree only when ninety days have elapsed since the petition was filed and since service of the summons (or its first publication) on the respondent (RCW 26.09.030).

simplified.text: No separate summary dissolution procedure in chapter 26.09 RCW; agreed cases use the standard statewide divorce forms and the same 90-day wait.

parentingClass.text: No statewide statute requires a parenting class; some superior courts require a parenting seminar by local family law rule.

uncertain: Response fee: King County lists a $310 fee for a counter petition but no fee for a simple response; RCW 36.18.020(2)(a) charges only the first filer and parties filing a counterclaim, so responseFee is left null.
Parenting seminar: King County local family law rules (LFLR) were not read; requirement left null.
King County fee page carries no effective date; read on 2026-10-08.

name: Arizona
feeText: Maricopa County Clerk of Superior Court: Petition for Dissolution of Marriage with or without children $376.00; Response/Answer to Dissolution $287.00.

otherFees.what: Summary Consent Decree (with or without children), Maricopa County
Petition for Legal Separation, Maricopa County

waiver.name: Apply for Deferral or Waiver (Maricopa County Clerk electronic application; deferral or waiver of court fees under A.R.S. 12-302)

residency.text: One spouse must have been domiciled in Arizona, or stationed there as a member of the armed services, for 90 days before filing (A.R.S. 25-312(A)(1)).

waitingPeriod.text: No trial, hearing or affidavit-based decree on a petition for dissolution or legal separation until 60 days after service or acceptance of process (A.R.S. 25-329).

simplified.text: Summary consent decree: spouses who agree on all issues can file jointly; Maricopa County charges $331.50 for a Summary Consent Decree (fee schedule). The 60-day wait of A.R.S. 25-329 still applies.

parentingClass.text: In a dissolution, legal separation or annulment involving a common minor child, the court shall order the parties to complete a domestic relations education program, unless the court finds it not in the best interests of the parties or child or a comparable program is completed (A.R.S. 25-352(A); programs under 25-351).

uncertain: Maricopa fee page was read from the Internet Archive copy (2026-08-13) of the official URL; the clerk's site returns 403 to automated clients.
Eligibility conditions for a summary consent decree (Ariz. R. Fam. Law P.) were not read from the official rule text; only the fee and its existence are verified.
Maricopa waiver page read from the Internet Archive copy (2026-09-23) of the official URL; it notes that full waivers are rarely granted at the start of a case (deferral is the usual outcome).

name: Massachusetts
feeText: Probate and Family Court: Divorce complaint (or joint petition) filing fee $200 plus $15 surcharge = $215.

otherFees.what: Motion in divorce actions during the nisi period
Complaint for modification of child support, custody or parenting time

residency.text: If the cause occurred outside Massachusetts, the plaintiff must have lived in the Commonwealth for one year before filing; if the cause occurred in Massachusetts, the plaintiff need only be domiciled there at filing, unless the plaintiff moved there to obtain a divorce (G.L. c. 208, § 5; see also § 4).

waitingPeriod.text: Joint petition (§ 1A): judgment nisi enters 30 days after the court approves the agreement, and becomes absolute 90 days later (§ 21), i.e. 120 days after approval. Contested no-fault complaint (§ 1B): no hearing earlier than six months after filing, then the 90-day nisi period.

simplified.text: Joint petition for divorce on irretrievable breakdown with a notarized separation agreement, no summons or answer required (G.L. c. 208, § 1A).

parentingClass.text: Not verified on an official page (Probate and Family Court parent education requirement).

uncertain: malegislature.gov refused connections on 2026-10-08; G.L. c. 208 §§ 1A, 1B, 4, 5 and 21 were read from Internet Archive copies (May-July 2026, § 4 Sept. 2025) of the official URLs.
mass.gov fee page read from the Internet Archive 2026 copy of the official URL (mass.gov returns 403/refuses automated clients). Fee for an answer not listed; responseFee null.
waitingPeriod.days = 120 counts from court approval of a § 1A agreement, not from filing; § 1B cases take at least 6 months + 90 days.
Affidavit of Indigency official page URL and the Probate and Family Court parent education requirement could not be read (mass.gov blocked, archive unavailable at the time).

name: Tennessee
feeText: Shelby County Circuit/Chancery Court clerk divorce filing fee not verified.

waiver.name: Request to Postpone Filing Fees and Order (Uniform Civil Affidavit of Indigency), Form 3 of the Supreme Court-approved divorce forms (Tenn. Sup. Ct. R. 29)

residency.text: The Supreme Court-approved agreed-divorce packet requires that one or both spouses lived in Tennessee for at least the past 6 months, or both lived in Tennessee when they decided to divorce (Tenn. Code Ann. § 36-4-104).

waitingPeriod.text: With minor children the soonest an irreconcilable-differences divorce can be granted is 90 days after filing (Supreme Court-approved forms instructions; Tenn. Code Ann. § 36-4-101). Without minor children the period is 60 days.

simplified.text: Supreme Court-approved agreed divorce forms for spouses who agree on everything and own no real property (with or without children).

parentingClass.text: All divorcing spouses with minor children must attend a parent education class unless the court excuses them (Supreme Court-approved forms instructions; Tenn. Code Ann. § 36-6-408).

uncertain: Shelby County filing fee not verified: shelbycountytn.gov court clerk sites return 403 and the Internet Archive was unavailable when tried.

Tennessee Code Annotated is published only through LexisNexis; statute sections are cited from the Supreme Court-approved forms instructions (read from the Internet Archive copy of tncourts.gov dated 2026-04-20, since tncourts.gov serves a browser-validation page to automated clients). The 60-day period without children was not read on an official page (the no-children packet PDF could not be downloaded).
waitingPeriod.days = 90 applies to cases with minor children.

name: Nebraska
feeText: District court Dissolution fee total $200.00 (mediation fee $50 and child abuse prevention fee $25 under § 33-106.03, docket fee § 33-106, plus the statutory add-on fees), schedule effective 07-01-2026.

otherFees.what: Proceeding to modify a decree of dissolution (legal services + mediation fees)

waiver.name: Affidavit and Application to Proceed Without Payment of Fees (In Forma Pauperis) DC 6:7.1, and Order to Proceed In Forma Pauperis DC 6:7.2

residency.text: At least one spouse must have actually resided in Nebraska with intent to make it a permanent home for at least one year before filing, unless the marriage was solemnized in Nebraska and a spouse has lived there since (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 42-349).

waitingPeriod.text: No divorce suit may be heard or tried until sixty days after perfection of service of process (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 42-363).

simplified.text: No summary procedure in statute; the Supreme Court publishes self-help divorce packets (no children; children without disputes).

parentingClass.text: The court shall order all parties to a proceeding under the Parenting Act to attend a basic level parenting education course, which may be delayed or waived for good cause (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 43-2928(1)).

uncertain: nebraskalegislature.gov statutes (42-349, 42-363, 43-2928) were read from Internet Archive copies (Nov. 2025) of the official URLs.
No answer/response fee appears in the district court schedule; responseFee null.
The Supreme Court's no-children self-help guide still says to bring $163, older than the 07-01-2026 schedule total of $200.

name: Nevada
feeScope: county (Clark County, Eighth Judicial District Court)
feeText: Eighth Judicial District Court official fees (effective October 1, 2019, still the schedule linked by the court's Family Law Self-Help Center): Divorce Complaint or Joint Petition for Divorce $299.00; Answer or First Appearance in Divorce, Annulment or Separate Maintenance Action $217.00 (components under NRS 19.013, 19.020, 19.030, 19.0302, 19.0303, 19.031, 19.0312, 19.0313, 19.0315, 19.033 and 440.605 plus Clark County Code).

waiver.name: Application to Waive Filing Fee and Order to Waive Filing Fee (Standard, or Joint Petition for Divorce version; each spouse completes an application)

residency.text: Unless the cause accrued in the county while both spouses were domiciled there, the plaintiff or defendant must have resided in Nevada for at least 6 weeks before filing (NRS 125.020); residence must be corroborated by affidavit (NRS 125.123, referenced in NRS 125.182).

waitingPeriod.text: No statutory waiting period between filing and decree appears in NRS chapter 125.

simplified.text: Summary proceeding for divorce by joint petition (NRS 125.181-125.184): jurisdiction met, separated 1 year or incompatible, no minor children or an agreement on custody and support, no community property or an executed division agreement, spousal support waived or agreed, and waiver of notice of entry, appeal, findings and new trial.

parentingClass.text: Clark County Family Court may require separating parents to attend a seminar for separating parents ("COPE" class); it is ordered case by case, not required by statute.

uncertain: NRS chapter 125 read from the Internet Archive 2026 copy of the official leg.state.nv.us URL.
Clark County fee list is dated effective October 1, 2019; no later schedule was found, but 2026 amounts were not confirmed by the clerk.
waitingPeriod 0 is based on the absence of a waiting-period provision in NRS chapter 125, not on an explicit statement.

name: New Hampshire
feeText: Circuit Court Family Division (schedule dated 07/01/2025): Original Entry of All Divorce Matters without Minor Children, including cross-petitions, $280.00; with Minor Children or Parenting Matters $282.00.

otherFees.what: Original entry of divorce with minor children
Petition to change court order without full agreement, or petition for contempt

waiver.name: Motion to Reduce or Eliminate Filing Fees and/or Costs, with Financial Affidavit (Circuit Court - Family Division, paper filing)

residency.text: Jurisdiction exists if both spouses were domiciled in New Hampshire when the action began, or the petitioner was domiciled there and the respondent was served in the state, or the petitioner was domiciled there for one year before filing (RSA 458:5).

waitingPeriod.text: No statutory waiting period found; after a joint petition is filed or the individual petition is served, the court schedules a First Appearance session.

simplified.text: Spouses may file a joint petition for divorce in the Circuit Court Family Division (no service needed); irreconcilable differences is a no-fault ground (RSA 458:7-a).

parentingClass.text: To complete a divorce with minor children, the parties must file a certificate of completion of the Child Impact Program (NH Judicial Branch, divorce with minor children).

uncertain: RSA 458:5 and 458:7-a read from Internet Archive copies (Nov.-Dec. 2022) of the official gencourt.state.nh.us URLs; the legislature's current host (gc.nh.gov) did not respond. Current text not confirmed.
courts.nh.gov pages and the fee PDF read from Internet Archive copies (2025-2026) of the official URLs; courts.nh.gov returns 403 to automated clients.
No separate answer/appearance fee found in the Family Division schedule (cross-petitions pay the original entry fee); responseFee null.
waitingPeriod 0 is based on the absence of a statutory waiting period, not on an explicit statement.

name: New Mexico
feeText: Filing fee for a divorce case in the Second Judicial District Court not verified; the statewide instructions say a filing fee is paid to the clerk when the case is opened (Form 4A-100 NMRA).

residency.text: At least one party must have resided in New Mexico for at least six months immediately before filing and have a New Mexico domicile (NMSA 1978, § 40-4-5, as stated in the Supreme Court-approved petition Form 4A-102 NMRA).

waitingPeriod.text: No statutory waiting period was found; the respondent has 30 days after service to respond (Form 4A-100 NMRA).

simplified.text: No summary dissolution statute; Supreme Court-approved Domestic Relations Forms (4A series) can be used for uncontested divorces.

uncertain: Second Judicial District (Bernalillo) fee schedule page redirects automated clients away and its archived copy has no content; filing fee left null.
NMSA 40-4-5 is published officially only on nmonesource.com (JavaScript app, not readable); residency taken from the Supreme Court-approved petition form 4A-102 NMRA that cites it.
Parenting class requirement (Second Judicial District local programs) not verified.
waitingPeriod 0 is based on the absence of a waiting period in the official instructions, not on an explicit statement.

name: North Dakota
feeText: For filing a petition for dissolution of marriage, annulment, or separation, $160 (N.D.C.C. § 27-05.2-03(1)(b)); answering a summons and complaint in district court $100 (§ 27-05.2-03(1)(c)).

otherFees.what: Motion to modify spousal support, property division, child support, parental rights, residential responsibility or parenting time

waiver.name: Filing Fee Waiver Request forms (N.D. Legal Self Help Center, "All Filing Fee Waiver Instructions and Forms")

residency.text: The plaintiff must have been a good-faith resident of North Dakota for six months before starting the action, or for the six months immediately before the decree is entered (N.D.C.C. § 14-05-17).

waitingPeriod.text: No statutory waiting period; an uncontested divorce filed with complete agreement paperwork is generally granted quickly and without a hearing (N.D. Legal Self Help Center). Rule 8.3 case management deadlines apply to contested cases (informational statement due 37 days after service).

simplified.text: Uncontested divorce: spouses who agree in writing on everything file the complete settlement paperwork together (N.D. Legal Self Help Center).

parentingClass.text: Under N.D.R.Ct. 8.3 the scheduling order may set dates for the spouses to complete parent education or divorce education; no statewide requirement was verified.

uncertain: ndcourts.gov self-help pages read from Internet Archive copies (March-October 2026) of the official URLs.
waitingPeriod 0 is based on the absence of a waiting period in chapter 14-05 and the self-help guidance, not on an explicit statement.

name: Oklahoma
feeScope: statewide (statutory components; county may add up to $10)
feeText: Flat fee for actions for divorce $183.00 (28 O.S. § 152(A)(1)) plus statutory add-ons in the same section: $6 Law Library Fund (B), $25 Court Information System (C), $10 OCASA (D), $2 judicial complaints/interpreters (E) and $10 records preservation until Nov. 1, 2027 (G) = $236; a county may add up to $10 for courthouse security (F).

otherFees.what: Ancillary proceeding to modify or vacate a divorce decree providing for custody or support (base fee, 28 O.S. § 152(A)(2))

residency.text: The petitioner or respondent must have been an actual resident, in good faith, of Oklahoma (or of a military post in Oklahoma) for six months immediately before filing (43 O.S. § 102).

waitingPeriod.text: Where minor children are involved, no final divorce order for at least 90 days from filing, waivable for good cause without objection (43 O.S. § 107.1(A)); no statutory wait applies when there are no minor children.

simplified.text: No summary dissolution procedure in Title 43.

parentingClass.text: In incompatibility divorces filed on or after November 1, 2014 involving a child under 18, the adult parties shall attend an educational program on the impact of divorce on children (43 O.S. § 107.2(B)); in other cases the court may require it (§ 107.2(A)).

uncertain: Total of $236 is computed from the components of 28 O.S. § 152 (read from the legislature's complete-title RTF); it was not confirmed against an Oklahoma County Court Clerk fee schedule (oscn.net refused connections). Other statutes may add fees.
No answer/response fee appears in 28 O.S. § 152; responseFee null.
waitingPeriod.days = 90 applies only when minor children are involved.
